extracted.intended_audience: journal editors and editorial staff (Sage journal editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal editors on designing, operating, and overseeing peer review processes (policy, reviewer selection, models of review, reviewer guidance, reviewer recognition, decision-making and turnaround).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal peer review policy (clarity and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your journal’s peer review policy should be stated on your submission guidelines. It should be clear what type of peer review is used (e.g. single-anonymize, double-anonymize etc.) and if peer review varies depending on the article type (e.g. editorials and letters might not be sent for external review). It is also important to state if not all articles are sent for peer review... It is also good practice to include an indication of the likely timeframe for reaching decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the peer review model, any article-type exceptions, whether some submissions will not be externally reviewed (e.g. out of scope or insufficient quality), and give an expected time-to-decision. Where language is a barrier, advise authors to withdraw and re-submit after language improvement or point to language-editing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single anonymized peer review (model assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single anonymized peer review is a traditional process where reviewers know authors' identities but authors do not know reviewers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include potentially more candid feedback and reviewers' ability to consider authors' previous work. Disadvantages include potential biases related to author identity (name, gender, institution) and lack of direct communication between reviewers and authors which can hinder dialogue. Consider bias mitigation strategies if using this model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double anonymized peer review (model assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Double anonymized peer review is where neither authors nor reviewers know each other’s identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: minimizes bias from reputation, gender, affiliations and promotes fair assessment on scientific merit. Disadvantages: identities may be inferred from context (preprints, conference presentations, research groups), so anonymization is not perfect. Weigh benefits for inclusivity against practical limits of anonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent / open peer review (model assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author’s and reviewer’s identity are known to all. In some journals, peer review comments are published with accepted manuscripts, alongside the reviewer’s name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: transparency, accountability, recognition for reviewers, facilitates direct communication and broader participation. Disadvantages: may discourage candid critiques (especially from early-career reviewers), pressure authors, reduce reviewer willingness to participate, raise privacy/confidentiality concerns in sensitive areas, and risk self-censorship. Consider discipline norms and potential harms when adopting open review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication review (model assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication review can take the form of comments/discussion alongside a published article or reviews of preprints on servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: broader engagement, transparency, iterative dialogue allowing corrections and refinements. Disadvantages: low engagement, potential delay in identifying flaws after research has already influenced the field, and limited diversity of reviewers. Use as a complement to pre-publication review where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferrable peer review (transfer of submissions/reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Sage journals facilitate the transfer of submissions (with author consent) along with any collected reviews to other more suitable Sage journals (Sage Path).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantage: faster assessment for authors in a more appropriate title. Disadvantage: some editors prefer collecting reviews independently and may re-review, so transferred reviews may not always be reused. Implement clear transfer policies and obtain author consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how inclusive your peer review process is: ensure content is based on scientific debate not personal agenda, is representative of diverse readerships, and that published language is inclusive and sensitive to communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt practices from 'Taking action on diversity' (e.g., broaden reviewer pools, consider anonymization, inclusive language guidance). Monitor and act to reduce bias in reviewer selection and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround times (time to first decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time to first decision can be a major factor for authors; competitive turnaround times vary by discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include expected timeframes in submission guidelines and work with your Publishing Editor to optimize time-to-decision. Balance speed with quality of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear guidance to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing clear guidance to reviewers will improve the quality of their feedback, giving you greater support in making editorial decisions and providing a better service for your authors. Some journals will supply a form for reviewers to complete; others ask reviewers to comment on particular aspects of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider structured reviewer forms or targeted questions to focus reviews on key assessment areas. Work with your Publishing Editor to design guidance aligned to journal needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper original?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask reviewers to assess novelty relative to the literature and whether the manuscript offers new insights, methods, data, or interpretations that justify publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of writing (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review should assess readability, logical flow, clarity of argument, and accessibility to the target audience. If language is poor but science promising, consider advising resubmission after language improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological soundness (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it methodologically sound; is the author’s theory or argument credible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate study design, appropriateness of methods, statistical analysis, and whether conclusions follow from methods and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics adherence (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper adhere to appropriate ethical guidelines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag ethical concerns (human subjects, animal welfare, conflicts of interest, data integrity) and check for required approvals and statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods reproducibility (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are methods described clearly enough for others to replicate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the level of detail, availability of materials, data and code, and whether replication is feasible given descriptions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation supporting conclusions (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it have results which are clearly presented and support the conclusions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate data presentation (tables, figures), correct interpretation, and whether claims are justified by results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct referencing (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it correctly reference previous relevant work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure relevant literature is cited, that citations are appropriate and balanced, and suggest missing key references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel contribution for the journal (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it make a sufficiently novel contribution to the field to warrant publication in your journal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask reviewers to judge fit to journal scope and significance of contribution relative to other work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for development (reviewer checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is not suitable as submitted, is it worth developing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should indicate whether revision could bring the paper to publishable standard and highlight required improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended number of independent external reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage strongly recommends obtaining two independent external reviews that have addressed the paper in detail, though the number may vary by field, topic and manuscript quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two as a baseline; consider a third or fourth reviewer for borderline manuscripts or when expertise gaps exist. Document reasons when deviating from the guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and substance of reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very important that the comments authors receive address the paper's content in depth, providing constructive criticisms of the methodology, the research and its presentation, as well as any other suggestions or observations that might help them in carrying out a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviews are insubstantial (focus only on spelling/grammar or are superficial) seek further review. Editors should ensure reviewers provide actionable, substantive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of provenance statements for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: For transparency, editors may wish to include provenance statements in published articles (e.g. 'Provenance: not commissioned; externally peer reviewed by two reviewers'), especially if the peer review of a particular manuscript differs from the stated policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaise with your Publishing Editor to implement provenance statements where appropriate; use to clarify any deviations from journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling revisions (editorial discretion on re-review)
rubrics_metrics.description: For revised manuscripts, if suggested changes are minor and the editor feels concerns have been addressed, it is not required to send the revision back out to reviewers for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only send revisions back to reviewers when necessary to reduce reviewer fatigue and maintain reasonable turnaround times. Use editorial judgment to balance quality assurance with efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating final decision to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating your final decision to reviewers is good practice and helps foster a sense of loyalty and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform reviewers of outcomes (accept/reject/revise) and, where feasible, provide brief rationale; consider thanking reviewers for their contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognising and rewarding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge reviewers’ support via thank-you lists, promotion to editorial board, integration with reviewer recognition services, and publisher-provided benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include 'thank you to reviewers' lists, promoting prolific reviewers to the Editorial Board, integrating with Web of Science Reviewer Recognition, providing 60 days free access to Sage Journals and 25% discount on Sage books for reviewers. Talk to your Publishing Editor to set up recognition options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer pool and track expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a sufficient pool of expert reviewers to enable submissions to be reviewed quickly and competently. Use systems (e.g. ScholarOne) to track reviewers’ areas of expertise, number of times asked to review, and speed/quality ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep reviewer keyword lists current, monitor reviewer workload and responsiveness, and use rating systems to identify reliable reviewers. Work with technology and your Publishing Editor to maintain accurate reviewer profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding the reviewer database (sourcing reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips for expanding your reviewer database: ask your Editorial Board for nominations, check reference lists in submitted papers, approach previous authors (watch for conflicts), include early-career researchers, and search databases/repositories (Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support inexperienced reviewers to build skills and loyalty; consult Sage’s Reviewer Selection Handbook for detailed strategies. Balance inclusion of early-career reviewers with adequate expertise oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on recommended and opposed reviewers (conflict rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage does not permit the use of author-suggested (recommended) reviewers at any stage. Reviewers should not be assigned if: the reviewer is based at the same institution as any co-author; the reviewer is based at the funding body for the paper; the author has recommended the reviewer (especially if only a personal email is provided and no institutional email can be found).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce strict conflict-of-interest checks when selecting reviewers. Do not accept author-suggested reviewers; perform basic online checks to confirm reviewer identity and institutional affiliation before assignment.
